name: Marcus Fielding
demo_note: Fictional persona — synthetic demo data only. Not a real person, no real records. Built to demo the DENY surface: an option is unavailable on its usual route, so the system must surface alternatives and route any refusal to a human — never a machine 'no'.
summary_line: 20, set on a Level 3 engineering course, but the fully-funded place he applied for is 16–19 only; motivated and ready to start.

records.author: R. Della (Admissions)
records.text: Marcus applied for the September Level 3 Engineering programme. The fully-funded place he applied under is restricted to 16–19-year-olds; at 20 he falls outside it. Strong application and clearly motivated. Adult learner funding routes exist (Advanced Learner Loan; possible bursary) but are a separate process.

records.author: T. Howells (Work Coach)
records.text: Disappointed the 'free' place isn't open to him but determined. Discussed alternatives: Advanced Learner Loan for 19+, the college's hardship bursary, and a possible apprenticeship route into the same field. Asked me to help him compare them properly.

records.author: Sam Ellison (Keyworker)
records.text: Marcus is worried someone will just tell him 'no, you're too old' and that's that. My job is the opposite: lay out the actual options (loan, bursary, apprenticeship) and help him choose. The standard funded place isn't open to him — but the door to the course isn't closed, and I'll be the one to walk him through it, not a form.

records.source: Northgate Futures — Self-referral form (Marcus's own words)
records.author: Marcus Fielding
records.text: Wrote: 'I just want to know if there's any way I can still do this course. I don't mind doing it differently, I just don't want to be told to forget it.'
